attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using arrays in your code to store, update, and access data in your projects.

questions.hint: What symbols always surround the elements in an array?
questions.title: [Select one] What symbol is used to store the elements in an array?
questions.correctResponse: Because there is more than 1 element in an array, brackets [ ] are used to store all of the elements and each element should be separated by a comma ,.

questions.hint: What other type of values can be stored in an array?
questions.title: [Select one] What type of values can be added to an empty array?
questions.correctResponse: Numbers, strings, sprites, or images can all be added to an empty array. However, all elements in an array must be of the same type. Be sure to declare the type when creating an empty array!

questions.hint: What does each function or property do in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Match one per answer] Match each function or property to its purpose:

statements.text: The ________ function can be used to add an element to the end of the array.
The _______ function can be used to find the index of the first occurrence of a value in an array.
The _______ property can be used to find the total number of elements in an array.
The _______ function can be used to remove an element at a specific index of the array.

questions.correctResponse: You can find many different functions to modify the elements in and gain information about arrays in the code completion tool. Just type the name of the array and a dot operator to view all of the possible functions and properties available.

questions.title: [Open response] What might you use an array for in a project?
questions.correctResponse: An array can be used to store lots of different data in a project, such as sprite images, numbers that can be used as background colors, or strings to share messages on screen.

subgroups.title: Arrays!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using arrays in your code to store, update, and access data in your projects.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about arrays and several functions available to help you create and update arrays in JavaScript. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Making a List, Checking it Twice
badges.description: Create and modify arrays within a program in JavaScript.

badges.title: Array of Sunshine
badges.description: Create an array in JavaScript.

badges.title: A Lengthy Calculation
badges.description: Calculate the length of an array.

badges.title: I Choose You!
badges.description: Access an element based on its index in an array.

badges.title: Objects May Be Larger Than They Appear
badges.description: Change the scale of a sprite.

badges.title: You’ll Fit Right In
badges.description: Use the push function to add an element to the end of an array.

badges.title: A String of Questions
badges.description: Use the askForString function to prompt the user for a string response.

badges.title: For Each Its Own
badges.description: Use a for element of loop to iterate through all the elements in an array.

badges.title: Search Engine
badges.description: Use the indexOf function to find the index of a provided value in an array.

badges.title: You’re Outta Here
badges.description: Use the removeAt function to remove a specific element from an array.
